storyTagline: The Eagles beat the Colts 48-10 in Super Bowl CLIII for a fourth straight title, the Cowboys end a 49-game winning streak, and Ryland Maxwell catches a record 53 touchdown passes on his way to a first MVP.

stories.headline: Four in a Row, and Maxwell Runs the Gauntlet: Eagles Rout the Colts 48-10
stories.dek: Philadelphia went 15-2, saw a 49-game winning streak end in Dallas, then won Super Bowl CLIII at home. Ryland Maxwell's first MVP completed a full set of offensive awards.

stories.headline: Mad Max Catches 53 Touchdown Passes, Wins His First MVP and Completes the Gauntlet
stories.dek: Ryland Maxwell ran for 1,692 yards and caught 71 passes in 19 games, 53 of them for touchdowns, and passed God Johnson on the Career Legacy list.

stories.headline: The Doctor Throws 68 Touchdown Passes and Is Super Bowl MVP Again
stories.dek: Bones Crawford threw for 5,131 yards and won his sixth ring. He also threw 20 interceptions, the most in the league.

stories.headline: Dallas Ends the Streak at 49, Then Beats the Eagles Again
stories.dek: The Cowboys won 35-32 at home in week 16 and 26-24 in Philadelphia in week 18. The Giants lost twice more.

stories.headline: Viennes Repeats as Offensive Player of the Year, With Wingo 47 Yards Behind
stories.dek: Keenan Viennes caught 99 passes for 2,041 yards and Calvin Wingo II 98 for 1,994. Nobody else in the league came close.

stories.headline: Akiem Brock Makes 75 Blocks, Twice as Many as Anyone Else
stories.dek: The Eagles lineman's card tripled in value. Snoop Dotson and Jacob Proise rose with him.

stories.headline: The Colts Reach a Second Super Bowl in Three Years and Lose to Philadelphia Again
stories.dek: Indianapolis went 13-4 behind River Kuechly's 1,825 rushing yards and 35 touchdowns, then scored 10 in the final.

stories.headline: Atwell Closes to 126 Tackles of the Record, and Spector Passes 400
stories.dek: Kyron Atwell is chasing K'Lavon Settle's 3,185. Siran Spector moved to fourth on the career rushing touchdowns list. Odell Hainsey retired 2 interceptions short.

stories.headline: Lazard's Touchdowns Fall From 39 to 18, and Cincinnati Falls to 6-11
stories.dek: Alshon Lazard played every game again, but the Bengals dropped from second in the power rankings to 27th.

stories.headline: Fox, Hainsey and Dwayne Skura Lead a Long Retirement List
stories.dek: Tevin Fox leaves with 69,973 passing yards and no ring. Dwayne Skura leaves with 4 rings and a Defensive Player of the Year award.

takes.headline: Maxwell Has Run the Gauntlet, and Sherman Brandson's Career Legacy Lead Will Not Survive Another Season
Ryland Maxwell's 53 Touchdown Catches Were Bones Crawford's Season Too
Bones Crawford Threw 20 Interceptions, and the Champions Got Away With It

Niles Canaday Has Caught 6 Passes in Two Seasons. He Is Still Not a Star.

didYouKnow.text: Ryland Maxwell is the first player on file with every award an offensive player can win: a ring, MVP, Offensive Player of the Year, Super Bowl MVP and Offensive Rookie of the Year. The MVP came last, in Y94.
Ryland Maxwell averaged 5.5 yards a catch in Y94 and scored on 53 of his 71 receptions.
Of Bones Crawford's 68 touchdown passes in Y94, 53 went to Ryland Maxwell. Keenan Viennes and Calvin Wingo II, the league's top two receivers by yards, caught 15 between them.
Akiem Brock made 75 blocks in Y94. No other lineman in the league made more than 37.
Ryland Maxwell has 11 rings, the most of any player on file and one more than God Johnson and Sherman Brandson. Dorren Skura coached him to every one.
The 2-15 Titans lost all 8 of their road games and allowed 657 points, and still beat the 10-6-1 Ravens by 16 in week 5.
River Kuechly ran for a league-high 35 touchdowns for the Colts in Y94 and caught 1 pass all season.
Rookie Reggie Deayon made 228 tackles in 21 games for the Colts, the last of them in the Super Bowl.
Ty Lock played his 300th game in Y94. Both of his rings came with Skura's Jets, in Y80 and Y82.
The Eagles' 49-game winning streak, ended by the Cowboys in week 16 of Y94, began after a 33-32 loss at Jacksonville in week 5 of Y92.

All 22 Defensive Player of the Year awards on league cards belong to defensive backs. The game credits a corner or safety's stop on a pass play as an interception, and the award rating counts each interception as much as 6 tackles. Jayon Queen leads with 2 awards.

Defensive linemen have 91 career interceptions in 8,168 games, one every 90 games; defensive backs pick one off every 9.4 games. The game scores a lineman's stop on a pass play as a sack: linemen have 371 sacks, defensive backs 1.
Retro Bowl caps each draft class by the coach's last record. After Skura's Eagles went 15-2 in Y94 (88.2%), prospects 5 to 50 of the Y95 class could rate at most 3 stars; a .500 season allows 3.5.
Winning shrinks the draft: in 71 of Skura's 76 seasons that fed a draft at the same club, his record capped the next class at 3 stars or less.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Sherman Brandson
vault.text: The General never flinched. Career Legacy 13,488, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Rondale Ikarras
vault.text: Flashy, loud, unstoppable, and he knew it. He was that guy. Career Legacy 11,508, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · God Johnson
vault.text: He changed his name to God. Then he earned it. Career Legacy 12,655, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Jayon Queen
vault.text: Two Defensive Player of the Year awards. Only one other player in this league has ever matched that. Career Legacy 8,686, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Tyrone Baugh
vault.text: Seven seasons, seven championships, and Tyrone Baugh has a ring for every one of them. Career Legacy 8,395, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Levante Hopkins
vault.text: The quiet one who did the dirty work. Career Legacy 11,355, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Mose Junior
vault.text: Some players chase rings. Mose Junior chased ball carriers. Career Legacy 7,694, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Dennis Baylon
vault.text: Seven trips to the Super Bowl. Seven rings. Not one loss. Career Legacy 10,341, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Charlie John
vault.text: Seven straight Super Bowls. Charlie John was there for every one of them. Career Legacy 10,021, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Ian Finney
vault.text: The first superstar. The Infinity Man. Career Legacy 11,316, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Bilal Tolbert
vault.text: No individual trophies. Four rings. And a sack record nobody has caught. Career Legacy 8,414, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Wayne Wilson
vault.text: Four hundred thirty-one games. Nobody in this league has played longer. Career Legacy 9,449, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Cairo Asanjh
vault.text: Some players chase records. Cairo Asanjh chased Ian Finney. Career Legacy 10,279, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Jahmyr Gibbs
vault.text: Mr. Incredible was here at the start, and he set the bar high. Career Legacy 7,802, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Zander Kolar
vault.text: Some defensive linemen are measured in sacks. Zander Kolar was measured in tackles. Career Legacy 8,619, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Ray Waller
vault.text: Never count out a man whose nickname is a promise. Career Legacy 8,863, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Tyler Pacheco
vault.text: Tyler Pacheco never needed the big play. He needed the ball, and he got it. Career Legacy 7,798, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Lukas Russell
vault.text: The Running Man started fast and never slowed down. Career Legacy 9,272, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Taron Hayes
vault.text: Eleven tackles a game, for 213 games, and two Defensive Player of the Year awards. Career Legacy 7,106, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Nick Bolton
vault.text: One of the originals, and he never stopped tackling. Career Legacy 8,684, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Michael Wilson
vault.text: Wayne's brother, and nobody's afterthought. Career Legacy 8,725, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Jackson Wardell Kline
vault.text: Tyrion Kline's son did not live in anyone's shadow. He built his own. Career Legacy 10,049, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Malakai Sawyer
vault.text: Some backs have a great season. Malakai Sawyer keeps having them. Career Legacy 7,694, Y88 class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · K'Lavon Settle
vault.text: Fifteen seasons in San Francisco, and nobody on a card has made more tackles. Career Legacy 7,702, Y88 class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Daren Teamer
vault.text: Eleven tackles a game is a Hall of Fame habit, and Daren Teamer has never broken it. Career Legacy 8,227, Y89 class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Kalif Suh
vault.text: A Jets linebacker since Y76, and the middle of that defense has rarely moved without him. Career Legacy 9,202, Y92 class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Jakeem Friend
vault.text: Linemen do not win trophies. Jakeem Friend won seven rings instead. Career Legacy 9,510, Y93 class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Lane McCoy
vault.text: Every time Denver got close to the goal line, the whole league knew who was getting the ball. Career Legacy 6,661, Y93 class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Damar Hobbs
vault.text: No defender in league history has taken the ball away through the air more often than Damar Hobbs. Career Legacy 8,362, Y93 class.
